intro.text: At the desk, a guest's money is called the bill. In Finance, the same thing is called a folio. In this video you will see the Finance screens, and what each one is for.

line.text: This is Folios, as the GM sees it. It lists every bill that still owes money, or is owed money back.
Folios is under Finance, in the menu.
Outstanding is what guests owe, and on how many bills.
Overpaid is money the hotel owes back to guests.
Overpaid guests are listed first. Nobody chases these, so they sort first.
Click a guest's row to open their bill, straight on the Bill tab.
Under Folios come Invoices, for the tax invoices after check-out, and Payments, every receipt, newest first.
Cashiering is your own cash drawer. It is the one Finance screen in reception's menu.
Cash deposits shows each day's cash to bank, what was banked, and who verified it.
Company accounts shows what each company or booking site owes, and what it paid.
Form three reports foreign guests. The check-in chapter explains it.
Online payments is not built yet. It opens a page saying what it will do.

outro.text: Reception reaches the other Finance screens with Find a screen. The next video opens a guest's bill.

intro.text: In this video you will open a guest's bill and read it, from the top line to the buttons at the foot.

line.text: Open In house and click the guest. Their panel opens. Click the Bill tab.
Due, at the top, is what the guest owes, with the nights still to come counted.
Each posted line shows its date, what it is, and who posted it. The first night is posted at check-in.
Charges to come are the nights the night audit has not posted yet, with their GST. If no GST rule covers the rate, it shows a dash.
At the foot of the panel, Charged is what is posted so far, with tax. Then Paid, and Due.
The bill is in sections: Room, Restaurant, Bar, then Other charges. Each section has its subtotal and its tax.
Every line shows its amount before tax. Under the sections come the total, the payments received, and what is due.
Total charges is everything posted, with tax.
Add charge posts a new charge.
Settle takes a payment. It is orange while money is owed.
Interim bill prints the bill as it stands.
Split the bill opens a second bill, for a company.
Check out stays grey until nothing is owed. The line under it says why.

outro.text: A button you cannot use yet is grey. Point at it, and it says why.

intro.text: A guest sent three shirts to the laundry. In this video you will post the charge on their bill.

line.text: On the Bill tab, click Add charge.
The window Post a charge names the room and the guest.
Choose the category. Here, Laundry.
Type the description. These are the words the guest reads on the bill.
Type the amount, before tax.
Leave Taxable ticked. It shows the GST rate this amount carries. Untick it only for a charge that bears no GST.
The box shows the tax in its two halves, central and state, and the total.
Click Post charge. The button waits while the charge is sent, so one press is one charge.
If the hotel has set no GST rule, the rate shows a dash, and the charge is refused. A missing rate is never taken as zero.
The new line is on the bill, with the date, the category, and who posted it.
A food charge, such as coffee from room service, goes under Restaurant.
Laundry and the rest go under Other charges.

outro.text: There is no discount button on the bill. A wrong charge is taken off with Reverse, in the next video.

videos.title: Taking a wrong charge off

intro.text: A minibar water was posted to the wrong room. A charge is never edited or deleted at the desk: it is reversed. In this video you will reverse it.

line.text: Click the curved arrow at the end of the wrong line.
The window asks: Reverse this charge? It names the line, and its amount with tax.
Type why. It is required. It is kept on the reversal's line, and the guest's bill never shows it.
Click Reverse. Keep it leaves the line as it is.
The wrong line stays on the bill, struck through.
The reversal is its own line, in red, with the reason. The subtotal and the tax come down with it.
A line is reversed once, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed. If the charge was right after all, post it again.
A line from a day the night audit has closed is corrected on Closed days instead. Once a tax invoice stands on the bill, only a credit note corrects it.
A payment is reversed only by the owner, an administrator, the GM or the accountant.

outro.text: If the curved arrow is grey, point at it to read why.

videos.next: A manager corrects a charge, or the rate

videos.title: A manager corrects a charge, or the rate

intro.text: This video is for the owner, administrators and the GM. You will correct a charge, and change the rate of a stay.

line.text: On a manager's bill, each charge has a pencil.
Beside it is Reverse, as reception has it.
Click the pencil. The window Edit this charge names the line and its amount with tax.
You can change the words the line says,
or the price before tax, or both. The tax stays at the rate it was charged.
Type why. It is required.
Click Correct the charge. The old line is reversed with the reason, and the corrected one is posted, in one step.
There is no pencil on a payment, or on a reversed line. On a closed day, or once a tax invoice stands, the pencil is grey.
To give the whole stay a new rate, click Change rate.
Type the new rate a night, before tax. The room's GST slab follows it.
If the figure you typed includes GST, tick Includes GST. The window then shows how it splits.
Type why. It is kept with every night it corrects.
Click Change the rate. Nights already charged are corrected to it, and nights still to come are charged at it.
It is all or nothing: if one night cannot be corrected, nothing changes, and the message names that night.

outro.text: A room night's price can be corrected, but not its words: they count its nights.

intro.text: In this video the guest pays. You will take a payment, split the bill with a company, and print the interim bill.

line.text: Click Settle. The window Settle bill says what is outstanding, and whose bill it is.
Choose the method. The list is the hotel's own ways of paying, with its default first. The amount is filled in with what is owed.
Change the amount for a part payment. Check what remains, and click Take payment.
The payment is listed under Payments received. At the foot of the panel, Paid goes up and Due comes down.
More than the bill is held as the guest's credit, but only after you tick that it is.
Cash above one lakh rupees at once asks for the guest's PAN, or Form 97.
When a company pays the room, click Split the bill. Choose the company, and click Open the second bill.
The bills then show side by side: Everything, Guest, and the company. The two-arrow button on a line moves it to the other bill.
Settle each bill on its own. For the company's, choose Bill to company. The amount goes to the company's account.
When the company pays, record it on Company accounts, with Record payment. Never in cash.
Interim bill opens the print preview. Click Print, and the bill opens on a page of its own, to print.
The interim bill is not a tax invoice, and has no number.
When nothing is owed, Check out opens. The check-out chapter goes on from there.

outro.text: After check-out, the numbered tax invoice is issued on Invoices. A wrong invoice is corrected with a credit note.

intro.text: In this video you will see your cash drawer at the desk: how it opens, what goes in and out, and how you hand it over.

line.text: Open Cashiering, under Finance in the menu.
Before your first cash, it says No drawer open.
There is no step to open. Your drawer opens by itself the first time you take cash. With nothing handed to you, it opens at zero.
If the last person handed you a float by name, it says so, and your drawer opens on it.
Only when a float is given to you by hand, type how many of each note.
Then click the button. It reads Count a float to open by hand, and changes to Open the drawer, with the amount.
During the shift, Taken this shift lists what you took, by method. Only cash reaches the drawer.
Money that was not a payment, such as a taxi paid from the drawer, is recorded under In and out of the drawer. A paid out waits for the GM's or the owner's yes.
At the end of your shift, count the drawer note by note, and click Save the count. It says if the drawer balances, or is over or short.
Click Close and hand over. If the count differs, write why. Choose who takes the drawer, type the float kept, and click Close the shift.
The rest is to deposit. The GM records the deposit on Cash deposits, and the owner or the accountant verifies it.

outro.text: A difference never stops the hand-over, but it must be written down.

intro.text: Here is the guest's bill in short: what to do, and when.

checklist.text: To see what a guest owes: In house, the guest, the Bill tab.
Something to add: Add charge, then Post charge.
A charge is wrong: the curved arrow, Why, Reverse.
Managers: the pencil for a charge, Change rate for the stay.
The guest asks for the bill: Interim bill, then Print.
A company pays part: Split the bill, and move the lines.
The guest pays: Settle, the method, Take payment. Then Check out.
Money that was not a payment: Cashiering, In and out of the drawer, Record.
End of your shift: Cashiering. Count, Save the count, Close and hand over.
After check-out: Invoices, Issue. A wrong invoice needs a credit note.

outro.text: That is the guest's bill. Thank you for watching.
